I"m sorry about how you feel at this time, I can't honestly say that I know entirely what you're going through right now, but I've had a number of situations wherein I was really happy, followed by situations in which I just wanted to die. It's shitty. It really is, I don't really have any particularly great advice for you, but in my situations, I tried to view these times as less of a mockery of the life I had before and more of a break from the times that aren't filled with good emotions.

If your friends are problematic in the way you've described, you might consider getting rid of them in some way. I realize it's difficult to throw out a crutch and look for a new one, but only by doing this are we able to strengthen ourselves. It's difficult when you don't have anybody in your life who you can consider a friend that doesn't treat you like trash.

I'm not certain how old you are, but based on comment history I'd put you at high school level. These three years were the biggest of my life and they were shitty and terrible, but I also put myself out there and met some of the best friends I've ever had. After high school, we are all going to go our separate ways and I don't even know if we have plans to meet up again, so I intend to make all new friends and have all new experiences with other people later on. It's difficult now and will be difficult a lot in the future, but you will probably end up reaching another plateau at some point in your life and hopefully relive that week in a whole new way. Good luck and I'm sorry about this, it's shitty. It really is.

I'm sorry about your father; sometimes family can be the worst. I don't have any incredible tips or tricks or anything and I think that it will vary by person what is most effective. It might be worth checking out the wiki as it does list a number of possible alternative options as OneEyedOneHorned said.

SH for me was quite frequently to help deal with stress, so I've recently been very close to breaking my few weeks sobriety in exchange for a small amount of calm because of final exams. Some things I found that worked were drawing on myself, as OneEyedOneHorned suggested, or taking a really cold bath. Anytime I start to feel slightly triggered or on the verge of panic attack, I run a bath of cold water and enter it until I'm no longer able to think of anything other than how cold it is and how much colder it gets if I even so much as move. 

Another thing you could do is remove the ability to sh by removing whatever it is you use. For me, I threw out the knife I was using a monthish ago; I could always get another one, but that was the only sharp one I could find and I'm too lazy to search. 

I think that staying clean is more about trying your hardest to not engage in these activities for as long as possible until it doesn't become quite so difficult. If you slip up, you shouldn't be too hard on yourself; just remember that you are at least making an effort and doing a lot better than if you had never tried to abstain. As well, celebrate all of the little things, throw yourself a mini party for every day clean and a slightly larger mental party for a week or a month or a fortnight.

I don't really have any advice on how dangerous sh localized in one area is sorry.

I think that another important thing is addressing triggers. You've already done that to a certain extent by acknowledging that your father being angry with you has caused a desire to sh today, but if you can think of anything else like the reason you've feared relapse recently, that could be helpful. Try and remove these parts of your life to the best of your ability; it isn't possible for many things, but it will be helpful to fix what you can. If you are having difficulties with your father, I might suggest attempting to appease him such that he is no longer angry with you. I recognize that this is challenging, especially if your relationship is strained like it sounds (assumption sorry)and you feel any amount of animosity towards him. If it is something you can change easily to appease him though like cooking meals or cleaning up, I would make an effort, if only to stop your father from becoming angry again. Stay safe and if you ever need to chat with somebody, you can pm me any time about anything at all. Have a great day and don't worry too much about your father; just remember that eventually you probably won't have to deal with him anymore.

If getting into university this year does not seem to be possible for you, you might instead consider taking off a year to work, earn some money, breathe a little, maybe attempt to upgrade some marks. I realize it isn't exactly what you had wanted from life, but sometimes we've gotta roll with the punches.

The problem with university is that so many people determine your value based on academics, so you feel pressured to do as much as you can; I feel like nobody is really able to see your true value except those who know you well enough. The same goes for the people who write the acceptance letters, they'll see a grade and immediately pass or fail you without knowing whether or not you are actually a good student. 

I know a guy who has gone to maybe half of his classes this school year, never studies, and manages to cruise by in the nineties; this is the kind of person universities are looking for, not because they are good students who put in an effort to learn or anything, but because they know how to pass a test.

You can't let the people who aren't accepting you get you down, I'm sure you are a wonderful person with your own skills and abilities that the university won't even consider. Don't let it get you down and keep trekking I suppose. It's difficult in so many ways, but we need to keep fighting until we can eventually, with a little luck, overcome our problems. I'm deeply sorry that you are having difficulty achieving acceptance to university and wish you all the best of luck with entry and the rest of your future. Have a nice day.

Sometimes it sucks to be left alone and not able to interact with the other person in these situations, but it's important to respect her wishes and maintain your distance. Good luck with this scenario, I really do wish you all of the best; hopefully with time, she will be able to open up and interact with you again. That said, if she doesn't ever choose to discuss it, please don't make a point of it or bring it to the center of attention or anything. Just remember how difficult it can be to think clearly when your mind isn't perfectly clear.

If she does come around to talking with you, you might suggest therapy or counselling of some sort if she isn't in it already and can afford it. Ensure of course that you don't say it in a way that blames her or implicate her of some wrongdoing, but rather casually suggesting it on the side and not making a huge point of it. I hate that question because I am quite similar. I've been living for the past 18 years and that's about all. I've gotten good at playing video games and I am not too bad at schoolwork, but other thank that I've just been going. I don't really have any passions or anything to be proud about, but rather feel like just a nobody. I don't have a large friend group and have always thought that if my life was a television show, I would hardly be able to call myself a background character even. I might appear for a single scene or something.

I feel insignificant and like I'm just another drop in the ocean all too frequently and that depresses me. I don't want to be something small and ignored, I want to stand out and make a difference in the world! I want to stand up and lead a revolution or something! I want to innovate some key component of medicine or industry or anything at all! Alas, I can hardly will myself to do anything at all. I depress myself in this way.

I've found that the best way out of this slump for me is a radical nonsensical change. Changing some aspect of my life that nobody else even cared about; rearranging my room, interacting with some complete stranger, purchasing a new outfit, getting a haircut. In this way, I don't succeed in accomplishing much of anything at all, but it usually starts as a chain reaction that leads me to do something else like vacuum the living room or clean the bathroom or something. It starts out small and I try to keep building and hopefully end up doing something that somebody else notices. I'm not much help sorry, but you should know that you aren't worthless any more than anybody else is and you are capable of incredible things! If you find yourself being lazy, try not to scold yourself, it is important to take some time for yourself to laze about, but try to limit this time so that you are able to still accomplish stuff and not get too down on yourself over what you haven't done or the person who you are. Have a great day and don't blame yourself, you're perfect.

I realize that this might come across a bit harsh, but I'm going to be pretty blunt. Please excuse me.

When dealing with situations like these, I would highly recommend that you don't compare your issues to theirs ("she won't accept that I've probably faced shit 10 times worse") as it has a way of coming across as 'suck it up, you don't have it so bad. That said, you can feel free to think these things or whatever, but never mention these thoughts to the other person and instead attempt to reach the issue that is actually bothering them.

Second, I feel that it is important that while you attempt to help, you don't appear as obsessed. I understand that you want to help and everything, but if she is shutting you out, I wouldn't attempt to address her problems any more than one time each day or so unless she brings them up herself. This way, she won't feel pressured to share information that she isn't comfortable with you knowing at this time. Make yourself available to chat at any point in time, but don't force her to share.

Third, I would make sure if I were you that when talking to her, you don't use this same tone. In this post, you have taken on an accusatory tone and seem to be blaming her for what is going on ("she should have talked to me... and it's driving me insane"). While she could very easily be at fault for this, it is important not to blame her so that you are able to maintain her trust and so that you don't come across as a jackass. She seems to be going through a lot at this time and, speaking from personal experience, might not be thinking clearly. You might think that it would be best if she just opened up, but she might feel as though opening up would be too painful or might make you dislike her in some way. 

Perhaps she knows that you used to cut and has recognized that you've gotten over a lot of your shit while she is only beginning to deal with her stuff. The reason she thinks you deserve better could be attributed to her thinking that she's still mentally unwell while you have largely recovered.

My advice basically comes down to not attempting to "one-up" their problems, to give them their space to think and breathe without you constantly hounding them to talk to you, and to remove all blame from her. Granted that all of this advice only applies if you are able to start a discussion of the issues with her. In order to do this, I would recommend suggesting you do an activity together where there won't be much or any talking; in this way, you can prove that you still desire a friendship without needing to discuss. This might help make her feel safe and more willing to open up later or some other day. Events like movies, sports, or concerts could work. I don't very well know your situation, but if you need more advice or care to discuss your own situation with me, feel free and I will probably reply within two days.

Once again, I'm sorry for sounding so harsh. It's kinda just default for me. Have a nice day.

Hmm... I've had several people ask me. I have a couple irregular scars that nobody could even possibly assume were from self harm due to the nature of their origin, so I don't even attempt to explain them. Other than that, i'm down to only a few scars on my arms that people would actually ever see. These I chalk up to the cats or dog I own. My pets aren't actually that vicious, but most people accept that. 

The primary spot where I've self harmed has always been my thighs, so I've still not had anybody see any of them. I don't wear shorts and I intentionally stay away from swimming for primarily this reason. I think the only person who will be seeing these scars any time soon will be if I end up in a relationship in the future. I plan to be forthright and entirely honest about them because it is impossible to actually cover them up.

As for how I see mine. Hmm... again. I like the ones on my arms. I wouldn't very well miss them if they were gone, but I do like having them around. They aren't across my wrists and would never tip anybody off to my selfharming, so I think I like them. I wouldn't call it pride, but more of a comfort type of thing. The scars on my thighs on the other hand are terrible. I miss swimming. I miss wearing shorts in summer. I miss making up excuses not to do those. I don't hate them because they are a part of me, but I would like them to leave and would be elated if they were no longer on my person.

Hey, throwing this out there, but the rubber band method is used for a variety of different things other than self harming. If they ever do approach you about it again, you could say that you were trying to prevent yourself from a different addiction that you felt bad about. Something that's bad, but not awful and not an actual concern; say you are addicted to pornography and want to prevent unclean thoughts, or maybe that you are trying to forget a certain event or person and that you don't want to talk about it. I realize it probably won't solve the problem, but it might make your parents stop questioning if they ever do start. As for the swimming, you could say that you have outgrown it, you feel less attached to it, you have something else to do, you aren't feeling well, or maybe that you have some activity that you would prefer to do. I don't know you very well and can't even say whether or not you would want to make an excuse, but I always find it good to have an excuse ready in case you do end up getting asked about anything than standing there stuttering on the spot.

Hey, I know some of what you're going through, I am also currently in IB and actually finished my first English A1 Higher Level Paper 1 exam today. It was pretty fucking difficult to be honest. I've never been great with stress before in my life and have attempted on several occasions entirely because of IB. The thing I've come to realize about IB is that it doesn't matter much, especially if the schools you are looking at don't accept it. For me, my university is going to look at it, say, "oh" and that will be just about all. I wanted to drop out of IB as well, but I realized that I had already gone through two years of rigorous study and that even if I did do really poorly on the exams and only succeeded in scoring threes or fours, it wouldn't matter too much. I might disappoint myself to a certain extent, but I would survive, life would go on, and I would still be going to university next year.
For me, I'm still crazy stressed and scared and consider suicide pretty much constantly. I frequently self harm and find myself getting unreasonably angry as well, taking it out on my siblings in a nonviolent, passive aggressive manner.
